claims.claim: During the Holocene humid phase, the Sahara supported permanent lakes and wetland fauna — hippopotamus and crocodile remains and depictions are documented across the region.
claims.definition: permanent water bodies and wetland fauna in the mid-Holocene Sahara
claims.measured_value: Holocene lake and fauna records, North Africa
claims.authoritative_source: Kuper & Kröpelin, 'Climate-Controlled Holocene Occupation in the Sahara', Science 313 (2006)
claims.notes: established paleoclimate synthesis; not a living record

claims.claim: Tassili n'Ajjer (Algeria) preserves one of the world's largest collections of prehistoric rock art — 15,000+ engravings and paintings, including giraffes, hippos, cattle herds and swimming figures.
claims.definition: rock-art corpus of the Tassili n'Ajjer plateau
claims.authoritative_source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tassili n'Ajjer (List #179)

claims.claim: The hyperarid core of the Sahara receives under about 25 millimeters of rain per year on average.
claims.definition: mean annual rainfall of the Saharan hyperarid core
claims.notes: climate normal; some core areas receive <10 mm/yr

claims.claim: The African Humid Period (roughly 11,000-5,500 years ago) brought strengthened monsoon rains, grasslands and lakes across the present-day Sahara.
claims.definition: Holocene wet phase of North Africa
claims.authoritative_source: Kuper & Kröpelin, Science 313 (2006); deMenocal, Nature Geoscience reviews
claims.notes: canonical dating for the strong monsoon phase

claims.claim: Earth's axial precession cycles over about 26,000 years and paces the strength of the North African monsoon — the orbital switch behind green Sahara episodes.
claims.definition: orbital precession forcing of the monsoon
claims.authoritative_source: Tierney, Pausata & deMenocal, 'Rainfall regimes of the Green Sahara', Science Advances 3 (2017)

claims.claim: The African Humid Period ended around 5,500 years ago; the return to aridity took centuries, driving population movement toward the Nile valley, the Sahel and the coast.
claims.definition: termination of the African Humid Period and human response
claims.notes: termination date and migration interpretation from the same synthesis

claims.claim: Green Sahara episodes recurred multiple times across the late Quaternary, paced by orbital cycles — the desert has flipped between green and arid states before.
claims.definition: recurrent humid episodes in North African paleorecords
claims.authoritative_source: Tierney, Pausata & deMenocal, Science Advances 3 (2017); proxy syntheses
claims.notes: recurrence established in marine and terrestrial proxy records

claims.claim: About 182 million tons of dust leave North Africa each year; roughly 27-29 million tons cross the Atlantic and settle over the Amazon basin, delivering phosphorus fertilizer.
claims.definition: transatlantic Saharan dust transport and Amazon fertilization
claims.measured_value: ≈182 Mt/yr leaves Africa; ≈27 Mt/yr reaches the Amazon
claims.authoritative_source: Yu et al., Geophysical Research Letters 42 (2015), NASA CALIPSO
